title: Microsoft announces Windows Server 2028 with hardened security
content_md: Microsoft has announced Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system, at the Ignite 2026 conference on Tuesday. This new Windows Server version ships with a hardened Server Core configuration by default and a new security baseline that allows admins to relax specific settings. "A hardened Server Core configuration by default and a new security baseline help reduce the work of establishing a secure baseline from day 1," said Neil Hinnant , Director of Windows Server & I/O Fabrics PM. "Trusted Launch extends protection to virtual machines, guaranteeing boot integrity across your VM fleet, and Confidential VM support begins a journey to support integrity-protected runtimes on supported CVM hardware." The list of hardened Server Core settings is extensive and includes: However, the company said it's still working on adding NTLM blocking, hardware-backed platform protection, print and RPC hardening, and more to the hundreds of security settings enabled from first boot. Windows Server 2028 also offers simplified administration and management at scale through Intune management for Windows Servers, bringing endpoint-management workflows for configuration, compliance, applications, and updates to eligible, persistent servers. It also improves performance with native NVMe storage enabled by default, NVMe over TCP and RDMA transports, and the ability to boot from ReFS.
